source_name: OTP Bank Nyrt. – Hírek / sajtóközlemények (corporate news room)
why_relevant: Hungary's largest bank self-publishes launches, modernisation programmes and named technology partners here; the only voluntary trace of OTP's vendor choices since its procurement never touches public portals.

source_name: OTP Bank – Befektetői közlemények (regulatory/IR announcements archive, by year)
why_relevant: Year-indexed IR announcement archive; material transactions, acquisitions and programme announcements land here before/alongside press coverage.

source_name: OTP Bank – Éves jelentés (integrated annual report hub)
why_relevant: Integrated annual reports disclose IT/digital capex, outsourcing arrangements and named strategic programmes — the deepest self-published evidence of technology spend at the largest HU bank.

source_name: OTP Group investor portal (otpgroup.info) – reports, presentations, conference calls
why_relevant: English-language mirror of OTP IR: quarterly result presentations and conference-call decks often name digital/core-banking programmes and their status — machine-readable slide text.

source_name: MBH Bank Nyrt. – Sajtószoba (press room)
why_relevant: MBH is the post-merger #2 bank running a large IT consolidation (MKB+Takarékbank+Budapest Bank); its press room carries dated, per-announcement URLs on partnerships and digital platform launches.

source_name: MBH Bank – Befektetőknek / rendkívüli közzétételek
why_relevant: Extraordinary disclosures ('rendkívüli közzététel') capture material contracts, mergers and programme decisions that never make the consumer press room.

source_name: MBH Bank – Pénzügyi jelentések / éves beszámolók
why_relevant: Audited consolidated statements and AGM packs; the AGM 'közgyűlési előterjesztések' PDFs describe the IT backend unification and branch-technology programmes in plain text.

source_name: K&H Bank – Sajtó (press & official disclosures)
why_relevant: KBC-owned K&H publishes releases on digital launches and results; the sister page /csoport/kozlemenyek plus its archive gives multi-year depth on system changes (e-bank, mobilbank, Electra).

source_name: K&H Bank – tervezett karbantartások (planned maintenance notices)
why_relevant: Maintenance notices name the actual production systems (e-bank, mobilbank, Electra) and their outage windows — an indirect but reliable reveal of the installed technology stack and migration events.

source_name: Erste Bank Hungary – Sajtóközlemények
why_relevant: Erste Hungary's own release feed; also aggregates relevant Erste Group items, so group-level platform decisions (George etc.) surface with Hungarian rollout context.

source_name: Raiffeisen Bank Zrt. (HU) – Sajtószoba
why_relevant: Press room of the Hungarian RBI subsidiary; publishes digital roadmap statements (self-service, AI development) that name delivery partners and internal programme names.

source_name: Raiffeisen Bank Zrt. – Pénzügyi adatok / jelentések (Tőkepiaci törvény szerinti jelentések)
why_relevant: Capital-markets-law reports and annual accounts of the Hungarian entity; a place where outsourcing and IT investment disclosures appear for a bank with no local listing.

source_name: UniCredit Bank Hungary – Media / Press releases
why_relevant: Local press feed of the UniCredit HU subsidiary, available in both HU and EN paths; group platform decisions land locally with named partners.

source_name: CIB Bank Zrt. – Sajtószoba / Sajtóközlemények
why_relevant: Intesa Sanpaolo's HU subsidiary press room with per-release static URLs (e.g. 250108-cib-orfk.html) and yearly archives back to at least 2019 — good backfill depth on partnerships and anti-fraud technology tie-ups.

source_name: CIB Heti Riport (weekly macro/market report)
why_relevant: Regular bank-authored publication; useful as a low-noise recurring feed and occasionally frames sector technology/regulatory shifts from the bank's own view.

source_name: GRÁNIT Bank Nyrt. – Befektetőknek (investor section)
why_relevant: Gránit positions itself as 'a DigitálisBank' and is the fastest-growing systemic-adjacent player; it discloses via its own site and the Budapest Stock Exchange, so this page is the entry point to its annual reports and disclosures.

source_name: Budapesti Értéktőzsde (BÉT) KIB/newkibdata disclosure store
why_relevant: Central hosting point for the filed PDFs of listed HU banks (OTP, Gránit, MBH entities) — a single crawlable store that resolves to authoritative annual reports and result releases even when bank sites reorganise.

source_name: MBH Jelzálogbank / OTP Jelzálogbank – befektetői pénzügyi információk (mortgage-bank subsidiaries)
why_relevant: Group subsidiaries file their own accounts, which disclose intra-group service and IT outsourcing arrangements that the parent's consolidated report abstracts away.

source_name: Bank general terms & conditions / Általános Üzletszabályzat PDFs (static file stores)
why_relevant: General business rules and card T&Cs name the channels, schemes and processing arrangements a bank actually runs (card scheme partners, digital wallet support, outsourced processors) — a technology inventory hiding in legal text.

source_name: Vendor-side confirmation of HU bank deals (iGCB/Intellect, Thought Machine press & fintech trade press)
why_relevant: Banks often stay vague while the winning vendor publishes the specifics; cross-checking bank press rooms against supplier announcements confirms named core-banking wins (OTP–iGCB Intellect Digital Core; Magyar Bankholding/MBH–Thought Machine Vault).

source_name: Portfolio.hu Banking Technology conference programme & bank/vendor interviews
why_relevant: The conference agenda is effectively a public roster of which bank IT executives are presenting alongside which vendors — an annual, structured snapshot of active bank–supplier relationships that no press room states outright.

source_name: GIRO Zrt. – beszállítói szerződések közzététele (supplier contract disclosure PDF)
source_subtype: statutory transparency contract register (PDF, periodically refreshed)
why_relevant: Line-by-line register of GIRO Zrt.'s supplier contracts (megrendelo/szallito, date, subject) under the Hungarian 'uvegzseb' transparency rule. This is the single highest-value primary vendor list for the Hungarian clearing/instant-payment infrastructure operator: it names IT suppliers (e.g. Cardinal Kft., R&R Software, C-NET Informatikai) with contract dates.

source_name: GIRO Zrt. – corporate site & Dokumentumok library (BKR, GIROInstant, GIROHáló üzletszabályzatok)
why_relevant: Operator of BKR (batch clearing) and GIROInstant (AFR central infrastructure). Its document library holds business rules, technical/service annexes and the list of participating payment service providers — i.e. the scheme rulebook layer that every Hungarian bank's technology must conform to, plus the participant directory.

source_name: KELER Zrt. – Közérdekű adatok (public-interest data) incl. közzéteendő szerződések
why_relevant: Hungary's CSD publishes a statutory disclosure structure including a contract-disclosure section. Confirms KELER as a disclosing entity; the contract register is the primary route to KELER's technology suppliers.

source_name: KELER Zrt. – contract register file (sensenet document API)
why_relevant: Appears to be the machine-served contract-disclosure table (Szerződés azonosító / dátum / megnevezés) behind KELER's transparency page; search extraction surfaced named IT suppliers (SLASH Szoftverfejlesztő, ROUTOLOGIC, Cardinal, DataCare Rendszerintegrációs, ÁBRIS Informatikai, SmartX Solutions) tied to the KELER Szolgáltatásfejlesztési Program (KSZP).

source_name: KELER KSZF (central counterparty) – Közérdekű adatok / Szervezeti felépítés
why_relevant: The CCP arm of the KELER group discloses separately; distinct systems (clearing/risk engines) and therefore a distinct vendor footprint from the CSD.

source_name: MNB – A hazai pénzforgalmi infrastruktúra / KELER Csoport oversight pages
why_relevant: The central bank both owns GIRO and oversees (felvigyáz) the payment/settlement infrastructure. These pages are the authoritative actor map of Hungarian market infrastructures (BKR, GIROInstant/AFR, VIBER, KELER group) and link to each operator.

source_name: MNB qvik – vállalkozóknak / szolgáltatói oldalak
why_relevant: qvik is the MNB/GIRO instant request-to-pay brand riding on GIROInstant. The merchant-facing pages point to the payment service providers and PSP/gateway integrators (e.g. SimplePay) that implement it — effectively a live directory of qvik-enabled suppliers and integration partners.
